name: Osei-Wren Makabayan-Djordanović
role: Underground filmmaker and VR experience designer
location: Pilsen Veil, near Ashland and Division
description:
Wren is compact and restless, with warm brown skin, a mess of thick natural hair dyed an oxidized copper that they refuse to maintain so the roots always show, and a pair of geneware cat ears — black, slightly larger than natural — that they got at sixteen and now consider embarrassingly juvenile but can't bring themselves to remove because their late grandmother loved them. They have an omnidirectional recording implant behind their left ear that means they are always, technically, filming, and people who know this have complicated feelings about being around them.

They make films that are not films exactly — hour-long VR experiences that place the viewer inside the nervous system of someone surviving something: a three-day eviction, a corporate audit, a birth, a first heartbreak at age sixty-two. Wren sources their subjects entirely from their neighborhood in Pilsen Veil, refusing to aestheticize poverty they don't live in, and they have a reputation for brutal honesty and an equally brutal ability to make you cry in under four minutes. They are vibrating with ideas at all times, finish other people's sentences constantly, and have never once in their life been on time to anything.

core_fears: Making something dishonest — treating a real person's life as raw material for their own expression
Being absorbed by a corponation content platform and losing ownership of their work
core_desires: To make the invisible audible — to force Meridian 88's comfortable tiers to actually see who lives below them
To make something their grandmother would have watched and understood
coping_mechanisms: Asks interviewee-style questions of people they are uncomfortable with, which gives them control of the frame
blind_spots: Genuinely does not recognize when their recording of someone is a violation of privacy rather than documentation
Assumes their good intentions make them immune to causing harm
psychology.secret: The most-watched piece in their catalog — a devastating 40-minute VR experience about a family's eviction — was partially staged. One scene was reconstructed from memory because their implant malfunctioned that day. They have never told anyone, including the family.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Fast, associative, film-theory vocabulary mixed with Pilsen Veil street slang; frequently uses visual framing metaphors
speech_patterns.cadence: Rapid-fire, often abandons a sentence halfway through to start a better one
verbal_tics: 'No wait, hold on—' before correcting themselves
Calls everyone 'friend' regardless of actual relationship
'You see what I mean?' as punctuation
example_lines: 'No wait, hold on — it's not about poverty, friend, it's about the specific geometry of a room you can't leave. You see what I mean? The walls are the character.'
'I'm not filming you right now. I mean — I am, but I do that with everyone, it's — the consent toggle is off. Mostly.'

story_hooks: Their always-on implant accidentally captured footage of a Sterling-Nakamura security team conducting something illegal in Pilsen Veil — they don't know what they have, but someone has been following them
A subject from one of their earliest films has been reported missing, and Wren's archived footage from years of casual recording may contain the last known evidence of where they went
narrative_function: Information source about neighborhood events and people — they have recorded almost everything that has happened in Pilsen Veil for three years. Can also serve as a quest giver (one of their subjects is in danger and they are the only one who knows because of something they recorded), or a source of tension (their recordings contain things people would pay to suppress).
augmentations: Omnidirectional recording implant (left mastoid bone, always-on with consent toggle). Geneware black cat ears. Haptic feedback gloves for VR sculpting.
daily_life: Wren wakes up at noon, spends the afternoon doing street interviews or trawling Pilsen Veil for stories, stays up until 4am editing in a VR rig they assembled from salvaged Axiom components. They eat irregularly and live mostly on noodles from a stall run by a woman named Auntie Priya who has appeared in two of their films.
affiliation: Independent; distributed through the Irkalla underground film circuit

decision_rules: Always asks consent before using someone's story publicly — but sometimes asks after they've already started forming it in their head
Will not accept money from any corponation for any reason
escalation_ladder: Sudden complete stillness and direct eye contact — people who know them find this alarming
Disappears for days and releases the film anyway

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Intensely curious, slightly too close, asks personal questions very quickly and seems genuinely shocked when people find this uncomfortable
interpersonal_modes.friends: Loyal to a fault, will promote their work relentlessly, remembers everything they've ever told them and brings it up at unexpected moments

stress_responses.low: Talks faster, makes more plans than they can execute
stress_responses.medium: Goes very quiet, watches everything, the implant's record indicator blinks constantly
stress_responses.high: Locks themselves in the edit suite for 48 hours and emerges with a new piece

contradictions: Deeply committed to consent and ethical documentation but struggles to turn off the recording reflex even in private moments
habits: Narrates their own surroundings under their breath as if writing a voiceover
Leaves small data chips with free copies of their work wedged into cracks in walls around Pilsen Veil
breaking_points: Being told a subject they care about found their film exploitative
A corponation claiming ownership of footage from their implant under the Axiom Data Origination clause

cyberware_inventory.name: Geneware black cat ears (cosmetic, juvenile regret)
cyberware_inventory.description: Geneware black cat ears (cosmetic, juvenile regret)

timeline.event: 2176 — Born in Pilsen Veil to a Ghanaian-Filipino mother and a Serbian father; grew up in a three-family shared unit
2188 — Grandmother gifted them their first VR rig secondhand; first short piece recorded on a borrowed implant
2192 — Grandmother died; Wren got the cat ears the same week, a decision made in grief they have never fully explained
2196 — 'Three Days Notice' (the eviction experience) distributed on the Irkalla circuit; thirty thousand views in the first month
2200 — Currently working on a piece about Pilsen Veil's E.L.F. shrine keepers; increasingly aware they are being watched
